the soma and the dendrite are interconnected via the ER network in neurons, and the ER Ca2 + store in soma acts as Ca2+ reservoir for the dendritic store.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the interaction of Ca2+ signaling between the soma and dendritic regions of neurons.
the regional interaction of ER Ca2+ signals between soma and dendrites through rapid Ca2+ diffusion.
the role of the ER Ca(2+)-store in the integration and conveyance in highly polarized dopamine neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ER network in neurons acts as a Ca(2+)-transporting tunnel, which enables rapid Ca(2+) diffusion between soma and dendrites, as a consequence of rapid luminal Ca(2+) exchange.
the ER in the soma acts as a buffer to the ER Ca2+-signalling in the dendritic areas.
the ER Ca2+-release mechanism and the ER Ca2+, as a Ca2+-buffer, are functionally integrated between soma and dendrites through rapid Ca2+ diffusion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ER network in neurons is functionally connected to integrate Ca2+ signals across the cell body and dendritic arbor.
the ER Ca2+-signaling network in neurons functions as a Ca2+-conveyor, and that this network plays a crucial role in integration of Ca2+ signaling in highly polarized cells.
Ca2+ signals are integrated in the ER network in a polarized neuron, and that the ER network in the soma and dendrites is functionally connected through rapid luminal Ca2+ diffusion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

ER Ca2+ signals are rapidly and bidirectionally exchanged between soma and dendrites in neurons through luminal diffusion, which enables the dendritic store to respond endurably to Ca2+-releasing input signals.
the ER network in neurons acts as a conduit for rapid Ca2+-mediated interregional communication, which is essential for integration of Ca2+ signaling in neurons.

the ER in neurons acts not only as a Ca2+-buffering compartment for local Ca2+ signaling but also as a Ca2+/dye reservoir for regional Ca2+ signaling, and that the ER network in neurons is a functional tunnel for Ca2+ diffusion.
